### Added
- **`components.cluster-manager`: the Agent Platform's cluster write surface as a chart component, off by default** (giantswarm/agent-platform#316; giantswarm/giantswarm#37637; bumblebee-plans#42 and #46; epic giantswarm/giantswarm#37639). One OCIRepository + HelmRelease of the catalog's `cluster-manager` chart (`>=0.4.2 <1.0.0`, `dependsOn: [muster]` — the floor is the first release that tolerates a cluster without the Cluster API group: `list_clusters` answers an empty list with a note, a dry run on a cluster that does not exist is refused naming it, `get_info` reports `clusterApi` and the real version) in model-manager's mold: the `cluster-manager:` block forwarded verbatim — the pinned Service name, the OAuth 2.1 resource server acting as the caller (`oauth.downstream`), the chart's own `MCPServer` CR with `forwardToken` and the `dex-k8s-authenticator` audience the kube-apiserver trusts, so muster registers `x_cluster-manager_*` and the portal's Clusters pages call the tools through muster as the signed-in user (MCP is its only surface: no route, no JWT policy, no proxy entry) — with `global.*` injected and `modelManager.namespace` derived from the platform's own namespace (an own value must agree). The connectivity chart renders the wiring from the `clusterManager:` block: network policies in both flavors (ingress from muster and the kubelet's probes; egress to DNS, this installation's Kubernetes API, the identity provider, the workload clusters' API servers — `clusterManager.networkPolicy.workloadClusters`: names, addresses, `ports: [443, 6443]` — and `clusterManager.networkPolicy.egress` on 443) and the render-time guards (muster off with the `MCPServer` on, a missing identity input, a bad CIDR, an empty port list, `clusterManager.flux.requireApi`). The two blocks travel to the connectivity release only while the component is on (`gatedValues`, vm-manager's shape); the default render is unchanged but for the roster entry. `examples/customer-bom.yaml` pins `0.4.2`; `make verify-cluster-manager` (`tests/verify-cluster-manager.py`) covers all of it; README "Cluster manager". The flip to default-on is a decision for after the first lab proof.
